messages.content: Go ahead and do the hotel checks now. I need the actual five-night totals, not estimates, and make sure the room will legally hold all three of us.

I’ll verify the exact bed setup and occupancy first, then compare taxes, mandatory charges, cancellation cutoffs, late arrival handling, and the added transit cost from each location before reserving anything.
Also, our flight does not land until 11:04 Friday night. I do not want the room released while we are coming in from LaGuardia.

The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central has a room with two queen beds listed for two adults and one 14-year-old. The hotel confirmed that configuration permits three occupants and does not require a rollaway. The current five-night charge is $1,885.00 before tax, plus $276.14 in taxes and a mandatory $34.00 nightly destination charge, including tax, for a complete total of $2,331.14.
That is higher than the earlier number. What exactly does the mandatory charge cover, and when does that rate become nonrefundable?

The destination charge covers the property’s daily food-and-beverage credit and enhanced internet; it cannot be removed even if you do not use those benefits. The rate can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. New York time on Tuesday, February 10. After that, the penalty is one night’s room rate plus tax, currently $432.23. A card guarantee is required, but the balance is payable at the hotel.
All right. Now check the Long Island City option just as carefully, especially the sleeping arrangement.

The Hyatt Place Long Island City has a larger room with two queen beds and a sofa bed. The hotel confirmed it for two adults and one 14-year-old, with no added-person fee. Five nights are $1,725.00, taxes are $252.57, and there is no destination or resort fee, making the complete stay $1,977.57. Its free-cancellation deadline is 3:00 p.m. New York time on Monday, February 9; canceling later results in a one-night room-and-tax charge of $395.51.
How do the locations work in practice? Include what we would spend getting to the Saturday and Tuesday plans, and getting back to LaGuardia Wednesday.

From Times Square, the Saturday activity is walkable and Tuesday’s is one subway ride; estimated family transit for both is $17.40. A Wednesday car to LaGuardia is about $75, so the location-adjusted hotel total is $2,423.54. From Long Island City, both activities require subway trips, estimated at $34.80 total for the family. The Wednesday airport car is about $45, bringing that option to $2,057.37. The late-Friday airport ride is already covered by the existing transfer allowance and does not change this comparison.
So Long Island City is $366.17 less even after the extra subway trips, correct?

Correct. The difference between the two location-adjusted totals is $366.17. Long Island City also gives you the confirmed sofa bed in addition to the two queens, but its cancellation deadline is about a day and nine hours earlier.

Book the Long Island City room. Put all three names on it, note that our daughter is 14, and tell them we expect to arrive around midnight or a little after. I want the confirmation to show that they will hold it for late arrival.

The Hyatt Place Long Island City is reserved for five nights, Friday, February 13 through Wednesday, February 18, under confirmation HPL-629417. The booking lists two adults and one child age 14 in a two-queen room with sofa bed. The guaranteed total is $1,977.57, including $252.57 in taxes and no mandatory property fee, payable at the hotel. All three guest names are attached. The hotel has acknowledged an expected arrival between midnight and 12:30 a.m. Saturday and confirmed that the card guarantee will hold the room overnight. Cancellation is free until 3:00 p.m. New York time Monday, February 9; afterward the penalty is $395.51. With estimated activity transit and the Wednesday airport ride, the location-adjusted lodging total is $2,057.37.
